function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Decision budget (20 calls) exhausted with the block still resting on the table. Three closes latched fully shut on air (gripper 0.016) because the pads were above the block; the fourth, at eef z=0.852, pinched it (gripper 0.155) but the hold was too shallow and the block slipped out during the lift-and-travel. Sixteen calls had gone into resolving the wrist-camera y sign, and the last two move_to calls executed only 3 and 13 control steps of much longer commanded moves, so neither a re-grasp nor a push into the bowl was reachable in the remaining calls.", "hindsight": "Grasp height: the pad gripping zone sits about 35-50 mm below the reported eef z. Closes commanded at eef z of 0.858 or higher shut on air over the ~20 mm block; the block was only pinched at eef z 0.845-0.852, so go low on the first attempt. A gripper reading near 0.15 means the jaws barely touch the block and the hold will not survive a lift; obtain a square, deep grasp before travelling. Camera axes: the front camera horizontal is world y and its vertical is world x, so the block and the bowl, which differ only in x, appear at the same horizontal pixel; the side camera horizontal is world x with -x to the left; the wrist image horizontal is the jaw axis (world y at yaw=0) with image left = +y, proven only by a 59 mm sweep - parallax below about 20 mm is unreadable, so calibrate once with a single large sweep. Motion: commanded targets are only partly executed; long moves were truncated to 3-13 control steps and left the hand 50-90 mm short, while a call that also changed the gripper got the full 80 steps. Re-read eef_pos after every call and never assume the target was reached; an intermediate gripper target (0.35-0.65) holds the previous latch state and buys extra arm steps. Geometry: table top z=0.80, block initially at x=-0.037, y=+0.004, bowl centre about 12 cm in -x at nearly the same y, so the two objects are almost collinear along x and the bowl is not in the way of the block approach."}
